finding: The Topbar's `Publish=ready` variant — the everyday, pressable CTA — is used by ZERO of the 15 numbered Shell boards; all 15 instance `Publish=disabled`, so the state a user is in for most of a session is drawn nowhere in the section that owns the shell.
evidence: Read of all 15 topbar instances (682:2657, 682:4901, 682:4926, 682:2738, 682:4951, 682:4976, 682:2687, 682:5001, 682:2763, 682:2788, 682:2813, 682:2712, 682:5899, 2162:11661, 2162:11839): every one returns {"Publish":{"value":"disabled"}}. Set 681:122 holds 6 variants (ready|disabled|anyway x open|none). Code: StudioHeader.tsx:607-613 yields `publish:"ready"` whenever `nextMove.blockedReason` is null, and lifecycle.ts:246-250 returns an unblocked publishMove for the ordinary case (online, non-viewer, publish flag on, reviews not required).
fix: Re-point the topbar instance on boards 199:2, 199:205, 66:4, 199:409, 200:2, 200:213, 66:225, 642:3696 to `Publish=ready`; keep `disabled` only on the boards whose own state blocks it (66:441 offline, 65:412 loading). STATUS 2026-09-05: coordinator reports this matches the topbar agent's independent finding; unfixed pending both accounts on disk (78 edges affected).

finding: A blocked Publish is visually identical to a ready one in the product: the board draws it at 50% opacity on gray, the code renders it as the full-opacity accent-blue primary with only `aria-disabled` to tell it apart — so the one signal a sighted user gets that publishing is refused does not exist.
evidence: Figma: variant 681:27 → btn/publish 681:42 opacity=0.5, fill=SOLID 229,231,235 (gray-200), text "Publish". Code: Topbar.tsx:295-321 — the disabled branch renders `<Button aria-disabled="true" disabled={publishBusy} size="xs" className={PUBLISH_BTN_CLASS}>`; PUBLISH_BTN_CLASS (Topbar.tsx:38) is `tw:h-8 tw:px-5 tw:text-[13px] tw:font-medium` — no colour and no opacity override, so flowbite's default accent fill stands, and `disabled` is set only while publishBusy.
fix: Add the board's treatment to the blocked branch (gray-200 surface / 50% opacity) while keeping it focusable with the tooltip — blocked must not read as ready. STATUS 2026-09-05: confirmed against the topbar agent's independent account; unfixed.

finding: `Publish=anyway` is dead on both sides — no board instances it, and the code cannot produce it. Two of the component set's six variants (681:46, 681:103) exist for a state that was deliberately removed.
evidence: Figma: 0 of the 15 boards select `anyway` (same instance read as SH-A-01); variants 681:46 / 681:103 render btn/publish 681:61 / 681:118 with text "Publish anyway". Code: StudioHeader.tsx:607-613 assigns only `published | disabled | ready`, and its own comment at :611 states "`\"anyway\"` is gone: the derivation owns the error re-label" — the "Publish anyway" wording now comes from lifecycle.ts:123 as a `ctaLabel` on the READY state, not as a topbar variant. Topbar.tsx:67 still declares `"anyway"` in PublishState and :171 still maps its label.
fix: Delete the `anyway` column from 681:122 and the `"anyway"` member from Topbar.tsx's PublishState + PUBLISH_LABEL in the same commit.

finding: Two publish states the code DOES produce have no Figma variant and no board: `published` (the 2-second "✓ Published" success beat) and `hidden` (no publish control at all — view mode, and a live site with nothing waiting to ship).
evidence: Code: Topbar.tsx:67 `PublishState = "ready"|"disabled"|"anyway"|"published"|"hidden"`; :282-294 renders the green disabled "✓ Published" chip; StudioHeader.tsx:772 `publish={viewMode.readOnlyView || !nextMove ? "hidden" : publish}` and :607-610 sets `published` from `publishOutcome`; usePublishOutcomeFlash drives the 2s window. Figma: set 681:122's only Publish values are ready|disabled|anyway.
fix: Add `Publish=published` and `Publish=hidden` variants to 681:122, then board the settled live state (which also needs SH-A-13's live chip).

finding: Publish-in-flight has neither a variant nor a board, and in code it is indistinguishable from the ready state except that clicks stop working — same blue, same "Publish" label, no spinner and no copy change.
evidence: Code: Topbar.tsx:322-333 — the ready branch sets `disabled={publishBusy} aria-busy` and nothing else; AquibraStudio.tsx passes `publishLoading={publishJob.uiState === "publishing"}`. Compare the sibling tool button at Topbar.tsx:246-254, which swaps in `<SpinnerIcon/>` while `previewBusy`. Figma: 681:122 has no busy value on the Publish property. Overlaps W-L-25 (in-flight states drawn as pictures, connected to nothing) — this is the prior fact that no variant exists to connect.
fix: Add a busy value (or a Publish=ready + busy boolean prop) and give the code branch the same spinner treatment Quick preview already has.

finding: The declared ENTRY POINT and the entry-point code disagree about the one thing a first-run user most needs to be told: the board says "Unsaved changes", the product shows a green dot and the word "Saved" over a project that has never been saved.
evidence: Figma 65:2 → topbar 682:2657 carries Save#698:0 = 697:452, inner instance I682:2657;698:525 State=unsaved; the board's rendered topbar text is ["‹ Exit","Bella Cucina","Unsaved changes","Publish"]. Code: useStudioState.ts:257 seeds saveState.status "idle" and :261 seeds isDirty false, so the precedence chain at StudioHeader.tsx:552-562 falls all the way through to `"saved"`; SaveStatus.tsx:81 then renders the literal "Saved" with the green dot from DOT_CLASS.saved (:72), and :99-102 silently drops the "· 2m ago" suffix because `savedAt` is undefined — so the claim arrives with nothing to qualify it.
fix: Give SaveState a `never-saved` value (or render the pill only once `savedAt` exists) so a project with no save behind it cannot show the saved state; board 65:2 already draws the honest answer. STATUS 2026-09-05: unfixed; coordinator flagged this as the finding they most want on record precisely.

finding: The entry-point board opens with no drawer and nothing selected on the rail; the code opens the Insert drawer at 280px with that rail item highlighted. The first frame of the product is a different shell from the board that declares itself the entry point.
evidence: Figma 65:2 Middle band 65:21 has exactly three children — Rail 2040:17794 at 0,0 60x748, Canvas 65:70 at 60,0 1080x748, Inspector 65:98 at 1140,0 300x748 — no drawer node; the rail instance is `Active=None`. Code: useStudioState.ts:225 `leftPanelTab` defaults to `"add"` and :235 `isLeftPanelOpen` defaults to `true` ("Always open on session start"), so LayoutShell gets `--drawer-open` and the grid becomes 60|280|800|300 (LayoutShell.css:71-77, :88-94).
fix: Settle which is intended and change one side — either seed `isLeftPanelOpen` false on a project with no saved panel state, or redraw 65:2 with Drawer 280 (pinned) + Rail Active=Insert and canvas 800. STATUS 2026-09-05: unfixed; coordinator flagged this as the finding they most want on record precisely.

finding: Board 12 Loading draws chrome the shell cannot have yet: a review pill on a status nobody has fetched, `Active=Layers` on a rail the code has on Insert, and no drawer where the code has one open.
evidence: Figma 682:2712 → Review=open, Save#698:0=697:444 (saved); Rail 2040:17837 Active=Layers; Middle band 65:431 = Rail 60 / Canvas 1080 / Inspector 300, no drawer. Code: StudioHeader.tsx:273-277 seeds `reviewStatus` to UNKNOWN_REVIEW_STATUS whose state is "none", and REVIEW_PILL.none is null (:136), so no pill renders until `fetchReviewStatus` resolves; the rail/drawer defaults are the same ones as SH-A-07. The phase this board depicts is the second of two (composer built, `projectLoading` true — ProInspector.tsx:315, StudioFooter.tsx:171); the first phase is covered by W-L-21.
fix: Redraw 65:412 with Review=none, Drawer 280 open and Rail Active=Insert, or state which loading phase it is meant to be.

finding: F6/⇧F6 region cycling silently drops the inspector on every no-selection state — the shell has 6 reachable regions, not the 7 the keyboard board promises, on boards 1, 2 and 5.
evidence: regionCycle.ts:12-20 resolves region 6 with the selector `.bdi-panel`. ProInspector.tsx renders that class only on the multi-select branch (:301), the loading branch (InspectorLoading.tsx:32) and the selected branch (:327); with nothing selected it returns `<InspectorEmptyState>` (ProInspector.tsx:320), whose root is `className={CONTAINER}` (InspectorEmptyState.tsx:79, defined :127) and carries no `.bdi-panel`. The shell's own inspector element is `aside.layout-shell__inspector[role=complementary]` (LayoutShell.tsx:131-148), which the selector list never mentions. The three boards all draw Inspector 300 as a present region.
fix: Point region 6 at `.layout-shell__inspector` (the region that actually exists in every state) rather than at an inner class one of four branches happens to render.

finding: No board draws a shell whose user is not allowed to edit it, and the shell only ever asks one permission question. A VIEWER opening /edit/:id gets the whole editing product — rail, drawer, editable canvas, an actionable Save button — and finds out on the first save, as a 403 toast.
evidence: StudioHeader.tsx:210 is the shell's only role read: `const isViewer = useEditorRole() === "VIEWER"`, and it feeds three things only — lifecycle.ts:106 publishBlocker, :201 the send-for-review blocker, and the IssueChip's readOnlyReason (StudioHeader.tsx:697). The canvas's read-only gate is the URL, not the role: StudioPanels.tsx passes `readOnly={readOnlyView}` from editorViewMode.ts:82, and Canvas.tsx:661-671 withholds handlers on that flag alone. The save pill stays a live button for a viewer — StudioHeader.tsx:745 gates `onSave` on `viewMode.readOnlyView` only, and SaveStatus.tsx:82 makes it a `<button>` on unsaved/error. The refusal arrives at useSaveCallback.ts:240-248 ("You don't have access to save this site"). RoleService.ts:39 already exports `roleAtLeast` for exactly this and the shell never calls it.
fix: Board a viewer's shell, and gate the shell's editing affordances on `roleAtLeast(role,"EDITOR")` the way PublishHistory.tsx:104 already gates rollback — disabled with the reason attached, per the P6 rule the header's own comment cites.

finding: "Unpublish site…" is offered in the ⋯ menu to every role including VIEWER, and the server requires ADMIN — a control on chrome that appears on every screen and cannot work for most of the people who can see it.
evidence: StudioHeader.tsx:798-809 gates the row on `viewMode.readOnlyView || !publishedUrl` and nothing else — no `isViewer`, no `roleAtLeast`. SiteMenu.tsx:208-209 renders `<MenuItem onClick={run(onUnpublish)}>Unpublish site…</MenuItem>` whenever the handler and publishedUrl exist. server/trpc/routers/sites.ts:425 `await checkSiteRole(ctx.prisma, ..., "ADMIN")`. The correct pattern is two files away: PublishHistory.tsx:104 `const canRollback = roleAtLeast(useEditorRole(), "ADMIN") !== false` with the comment "non-admins see the button disabled with 'Ask an admin to roll back', never hidden" — for rollback, sites.ts:485, the same ADMIN gate.
fix: Gate the Unpublish row on `roleAtLeast(role,"ADMIN")` and render it disabled with "Ask an admin to unpublish" for everyone else.

finding: The Topbar component has no node for the tool cluster the shell renders on every screen, so board 6 · Comment mode cannot draw its own subject — the pressed Comments toggle is the shell's only comment-mode affordance and no board draws it.
evidence: Component 681:122's variant 681:26 has nine direct children: btn/exit 698:428, site name 680:11, pill/saved 698:445, pill/in 680:15, spacer 680:18, presence 692:473, btn/notifications 698:430, btn/publish 680:22, btn/more 698:438 — no Quick preview, no Comments, no IssueChip, and no gap between spacer (x554 w680, ends 1234) and presence (x1246) to hold them. Code: Topbar.tsx:12-13 names "tools" as one of the ten children of the component and :244-263 renders Quick preview + Comments + IssueChip; the pressed state is `pressed={Boolean(tools.commentsPressed)}` at :257, driven from StudioHeader.tsx:229-233 via `ui:comment-mode-changed`. Board 200:2's middle band (200:21) is Rail/Drawer/Canvas/Inspector only — the comment state has no chrome representation anywhere on it. Overlaps W-L-13, which reports the same controls as unwired in the prototype; this is the prior fact that three of them are not in the component at all.
fix: Add the tool cluster to 681:122 with a Comments pressed variant, then re-point board 200:2 at it.

finding: The live-site chip has no node in the Topbar component and no board, so the terminal state of the product's own loop — published, nothing waiting — is undrawn in the section that owns the shell.
evidence: Topbar.tsx:141-151 documents the chip as load-bearing: "on a site that is live with nothing waiting, the derivation returns no next move and the CTA disappears. Without this chip, 'your site is live' would have no representation in the shell at all, and a finished site would look identical to one that was never published." It renders at :217-236 as `● Live · <host>`. lifecycle.ts:246 returns `null` for exactly that state and StudioHeader.tsx:772 turns that into `publish="hidden"`. Component 681:122 has no such child (see SH-A-12's child list) and no board carries one.
fix: Add the live chip to 681:122 and board the settled live state alongside SH-A-04's `hidden` publish variant.

finding: Six review states in code collapse to two Figma values, and 14 of the 15 boards pin the property to `open` — so "Changes requested", the one review state that turns the CTA into a different verb and the pill amber, is drawn on no shell board.
evidence: Code: REVIEW_PILL (StudioHeader.tsx:135-142) maps none|pending|opened-not-acted|changes-requested|approved|approved-edited-since; three tones at Topbar.tsx:351-355 with `warning` the only visually distinct one; a dynamic "Approved by <name> · 2d ago" label at StudioHeader.tsx:711-716; lifecycle.ts:224-233 turns changes-requested into a different CTA entirely (`kind:"open-feedback"`, label "Open feedback"). Figma: 681:122 varies only `Review: open|none`; the instance read shows `open` on all boards except 65:2, which is `none`.
fix: Either add a Review tone/state property to 681:122, or board the changes-requested and approved shells as their own states — the CTA verb changes with them, so they are shell states, not pill skins.

finding: Full-page mode has no board. Opening Settings — or Media in library mode — deletes drawer, canvas AND inspector and replaces them with one full-width surface, a fourth middle-band arrangement none of the 15 boards shows.
evidence: StudioPanels.tsx:255-258 `effectiveFullPageMode = isFullPageMode || getTabMode(activeTabId)==="fullpage" || (activeTabId==="assets" && mediaFullPage)`; tabsConfig.ts:199 marks `settings` as the fullpage tab; StudioPanels.tsx:418-420 passes it to LayoutShell, and LayoutShell.css:311-320 sets `visibility:hidden; position:absolute; width:0` on `.layout-shell__drawer`, `__canvas` and `__inspector` under `.layout-shell--fullpage`. The result is Rail 60 + FullPage 1380. All 15 boards draw a canvas.
fix: Board the fullpage arrangement once as a shell state (Rail 60 · FullPage 1380 · Footer 32); the module boards inside it can then instance it.

finding: The collapsed inspector has no board, and it is not a transient — it is a user toggle remembered in localStorage, so it is the shell a returning user opens into.
evidence: StudioPanels.tsx:232-243: `inspectorShown` initialises from `localStorage.getItem("buildrick-inspector-shown") !== "false"` and `toggleInspector` writes it back; :422 `inspectorOpen={!readOnlyView && !effectiveFullPageMode && inspectorShown}`; the control lives on the canvas (Canvas.tsx:829-830 `inspectorOpen` / `onToggleInspector`). LayoutShell.css:71-77 then gives the 4th column 0px, so the canvas runs to 1380 (drawer closed) or 1100 (drawer open). Every non-preview board among the 15 draws Inspector 300.
fix: Board Rail + Canvas with no inspector, and Rail + Drawer + Canvas with no inspector — the toggle produces both.

finding: View mode (`?view=readonly`) has no board in the Shell section, and it is the largest single change the product makes to the shell — rail, drawer and inspector all gone, canvas full width, no save pill, no publish control, and the leftmost button doing something else entirely.
evidence: editorViewMode.ts:82 `readOnlyView = q.get("view") === "readonly"`. StudioPanels.tsx:427/491 return null for the Sidebar and Inspector slots; :223 adds `html.bk-read-only-view`, which LayoutShell.css:70 uses to collapse `--layout-rail-width` to 0. StudioHeader.tsx:739-740 relabels exit to "‹ Back to editing" and points it at `toggleReadOnlyView`; :743-745 omits `save` and `onSave`; :772 forces `publish="hidden"`; :686-698 reduces `tools` to Comments alone; :785-812 withholds every SiteMenu build door. Board 65:211 (state 7 Preview) is a different surface — a sandboxed iframe overlay (PreviewOverlay.tsx:70-116), not this mode.
fix: Board view mode as a shell state; it is reachable from the ⋯ menu (StudioHeader.tsx:811 onToggleReadOnlyView) so it is a door users press, not a URL trick.

finding: Board 7 Preview and the shipped preview disagree about what sits under the topbar: the board draws Canvas 1440 + a Done pill and nothing else; the code puts a 40px device bar with a breakpoint switcher above the page.

Code: PreviewOverlay.tsx:43-45 DEVICE_BAR_CLASS is a 40-tall gray-50 strip with a hairline, rendered at :99-101 with `<BreakpointSwitcher labelled …>`; the file's own header (:10-16) attributes it to board 807:8663. So two boards describe state 7 and the Shell section's own board is the stale one.
fix: Add the device bar to 65:211 (or record 807:8663 as the authority for state 7 in boards.json).

finding: The rail has a third visual state the component cannot express and no board draws — "last active, drawer closed" — and in that state the rail's visual and accessible answers contradict each other.
evidence: LeftSidebar.tsx:151 keeps `ls-btn--active` and adds `ls-btn--last` when `!drawerOpen && isSelectedTab`; LeftSidebar.css:191-198 (`.ls-btn--last { background: var(--bk-bg-subtle) }`) wins over :179-182 on source order at equal specificity, so the button stays visibly highlighted in a dim tone. But :154 sets `aria-selected={isVisibleActive}` where `isVisibleActive = isSelectedTab && drawerOpen` (:137) — false — so a screen reader is told nothing is selected while the screen shows something is. Board 199:409 instances Rail 2040:18145 `Active=None`; set 2034:8519's seven values are None|Insert|Layers|Pages|Media|Content|Brand, with no dim/last value.

finding: The board named "Shell state 13 · Presence (multiplayer)" does not draw presence: its topbar instances `Presence State=solo`, which is a 1x24 frame with zero children. Four of the Presence set's five states are used by no board at all.
evidence: Figma: 642:3696 → topbar 682:5899 → I682:5899;692:474 `{"State":{"value":"solo"}}`; set 692:472 holds State=solo|few|many|reconnecting|offline; the solo variant measures w1 h24 with an empty children list. All 15 boards carry the same solo instance. Code: StudioHeader.tsx:748-763 passes `presence` only when `collabOn && collaborationState !== "disconnected"`, with `max: 2` (two faces then "+N") and connection live|reconnecting — the `[design-ahead]` tag correctly says this is not shipped, but the board still needs to depict its own subject.
fix: Swap 682:5899's Presence instance to `State=few` or `many` so the presence board shows presence; board `reconnecting` alongside it, since the code has a distinct treatment for it.

finding: Dismissing the conflict modal strands the shell: the save status stays `conflict` with no way to act on it, the chip is deliberately not a button in that state, and the modal has no reopen door.
evidence: useSaveCallback.ts:140-147 sets `status: "conflict"` and nothing clears it except a later successful save (:125); useComposerInit.ts:557 does the same from autosave. StudioHeader.tsx:552-558 ranks conflict above `unsaved`, so the chip reads "Conflict — reload" (SaveStatus.tsx:44) through every subsequent edit. SaveStatus.tsx:82 `actionable = Boolean(onRetry) && (state === "error" || state === "unsaved")` — conflict is a plain `<span>`. AquibraStudio.tsx:684-690 wires ConflictModal's `onClose` to `setConflict(null)` only, and the modal is opened solely by the `SAVE_CONFLICT_EVENT` listener at :350-356, which will not re-fire without another save attempt. Board 66:640 draws the modal open and says nothing about the state after ✕.
fix: Either make the conflict chip a door back to the modal, or keep the modal non-dismissible until one of its three outcomes is taken (the board's three actions are the only exits).

finding: Every one of the 15 boards carries exactly one save value, so the combination states the precedence chain exists to resolve are drawn nowhere — and the chain silently deletes the losing half.
evidence: StudioHeader.tsx:552-562 orders offline > saving > conflict > error > unsaved > saved. Consequences: offline AND dirty renders exactly board 66:441 with no unsaved signal at all (the exit guard is the only place the combination surfaces — StudioHeader.tsx:399 `if (offline && isDirty) return setExitDialog({kind:"risky"})`, drawn on 1172:4816); an autosave in flight hides a standing conflict, because `saving` outranks it; and an AI run that mutates the document flips the chip to `unsaved` while board 66:225 (AI agent run) draws `saved` — the shell has no AI-run indicator of its own (StudioPanels.tsx:296-299 only swaps the inspector's contents). Review-blocked publish plus a save failure is likewise undrawn: lifecycle.ts:210-214 disables the CTA on the review round while the save chip is independently in `error`.
fix: Board at least offline+unsaved and review-blocked+save-failed; they are the two the user is most likely to hit and the ones where losing the second signal costs work.

finding: The three newest boards have no caption, so the section's own labelling stops at state 12 — states 13, 14 and 15 are the only numbered boards a reader cannot identify from the caption row.
fix: Add three `caption/` nodes matching the existing pattern.

finding: A second, unreachable copy of the shell's save/dirty/undo state sits in the hooks folder — the exact drift StudioHeader's own prop comment warns about ("this was the fifth copy of that union, and each copy is a place the set can silently fall behind").
evidence: editor/shell/hooks/useSaveState.ts is 55 lines defining `SaveState`-shaped state identical to useStudioState.ts:257-265, declared as `function useSaveState()` at :31 with no `export` on the function, no default export, no entry in hooks/index.ts, and zero imports repo-wide (`grep -rn useSaveState src/` returns only the file itself). It also predates the `conflict` status, so it is already behind the union it duplicates.
fix: Delete the file — useStudioState is the SSOT.
